overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of how to divide writing and analysis work between yourself and AI. You'll be asked about what controlled studies found, the four roles for AI in writing, analysis from your own sources, and roles for AI in teaching work.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Three studies of professionals using AI found gains in speed and quality on some tasks. Which workers tended to gain the most?

options.html: The most experienced workers, who knew how to direct the tool
options.text: The most experienced workers, who knew how to direct the tool
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. In one study the most experienced workers saw small declines in quality. The largest gains went to less experienced and lower-performing workers, a pattern called skill leveling.

options.html: Workers who had already used AI for more than a year
options.text: Workers who had already used AI for more than a year
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The studies didn't compare workers by prior AI use. The largest gains went to less experienced and lower-performing workers, a pattern called skill leveling.

options.html: Less experienced and lower-performing workers
options.text: Less experienced and lower-performing workers
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! All three studies found the largest gains among weaker or newer workers. This narrowing of the gap is called skill leveling.

options.html: Workers in technical jobs, whatever their experience
options.text: Workers in technical jobs, whatever their experience
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The studies covered writing, customer support, and consulting, and didn't single out technical jobs. The largest gains went to less experienced and lower-performing workers, a pattern called skill leveling.

forms.stemHtml: A director has to write a recommendation that she will defend in front of her board. Which use of AI keeps the most of the reasoning with her?

options.html: She writes the draft and asks the AI for objections
options.text: She writes the draft and asks the AI for objections
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! With AI as critic, she builds the argument and decides which criticisms hold. The reasoning stays hers.

options.html: The AI writes the draft and she edits it for tone and style
options.text: The AI writes the draft and she edits it for tone and style
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A draft from the AI sets the structure and conclusion before she has thought. Writing the draft herself and asking the AI for objections keeps the reasoning with her.

options.html: The AI writes the draft and then tightens its own wording
options.text: The AI writes the draft and then tightens its own wording
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Here the AI is both drafter and editor, and none of the reasoning is hers. Writing the draft herself and asking the AI for objections keeps the reasoning with her.

options.html: The AI drafts three versions and she picks the best one
options.text: The AI drafts three versions and she picks the best one
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Choosing among drafts still means reacting to frames the AI set. Writing the draft herself and asking the AI for objections keeps the reasoning with her.

forms.stemHtml: You give an AI assistant a set of interview notes and ask it to list the main complaints. What makes its list quickest to check?

options.html: Asking it to state how confident it is in each complaint
options.text: Asking it to state how confident it is in each complaint
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A model's stated confidence isn't evidence that a point is in your notes. Asking for the supporting passage lets you check each point against the original.

options.html: Asking it to list the complaints a second time and compare
options.text: Asking it to list the complaints a second time and compare
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Two lists from the same model can share the same misreading. Asking for the supporting passage lets you check each point against the original.

options.html: Asking it to keep the list to five complaints or fewer
options.text: Asking it to keep the list to five complaints or fewer
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A shorter list is quicker to read, and no easier to verify. Asking for the supporting passage lets you check each point against the original.

options.html: Asking it to quote the passage that supports each point
options.text: Asking it to quote the passage that supports each point
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! With a passage for each point, you can find it in your notes and see whether it says what the model claims. The passage has to be found in the original, since a model can misquote.

forms.stemHtml: In an analysis done with AI from your own documents, which steps carry the judgment and are best kept as your own? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Deciding what question the analysis should answer
options.text: Deciding what question the analysis should answer
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The question sets what counts as an answer, and it depends on what you and your organization need.

options.html: Pulling every date and figure out of the documents
options.text: Pulling every date and figure out of the documents
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. This is extraction, a mechanical step a model does quickly. You check a sample of it against the documents.

options.html: Deciding which findings matter more than others
options.text: Deciding which findings matter more than others
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Weighing depends on things the model doesn't know, such as your organization's history and who had the fullest view.

options.html: Deciding what the findings mean and what to do
options.text: Deciding what the findings mean and what to do
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The conclusion is yours to make and to answer for. The model's reading can be one input.

forms.stemHtml: Two educators proposed seven roles a teacher might assign to AI in student work, such as tutor and simulator. What do they require of the student in every role?

options.html: To use the AI only while the teacher is watching
options.text: To use the AI only while the teacher is watching
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The proposal doesn't depend on supervision. It requires the student to stay the human in the loop: to check the AI's output and answer for the final work.

options.html: To check the AI's output and answer for the work
options.text: To check the AI's output and answer for the work
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The authors ask students to remain the human in the loop. Each role carries a risk of error, so the student oversees the output and is responsible for the result.

options.html: To accept the AI's feedback as they would a teacher's
options.text: To accept the AI's feedback as they would a teacher's
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Accepting feedback without examining it is one of the risks the authors name. They require the student to stay the human in the loop: to check the AI's output and answer for the final work.

options.html: To finish a course on how AI models are trained first
options.text: To finish a course on how AI models are trained first
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The proposal sets no such condition. It requires the student to stay the human in the loop: to check the AI's output and answer for the final work.

title: Thinking, writing, and analysis with AI
